intended_object: Given a split monomorphism i : A → M with retraction r : M → A (r ∘ i = id), this is the canonical projection of M onto ker r along im i, x ↦ x − i(r x). Inferred from the docstring, the name and the `_apply` lemma.
explanation:
The body is `codRestrict (ker r) (id − i ∘ r)`, so it sends x to x − i(r x). The membership proof checks that r(x − i r x) = r x − r x = 0. This is exactly the standard projection of M onto ker r along the complement im i in the decomposition M ≅ ker r ⊕ A.

The setting is general enough. R only needs to be a semiring and A an additive commutative monoid. M must be an additive commutative group because the formula uses subtraction.

Mathlib's `Submodule.projectionOnto` gives the same map, but it needs a proof of `IsCompl (ker r) (range i)` as input. Mathlib has no definition that builds the projection directly from a retraction. So this definition is not a narrower copy of an existing Mathlib construction. It is a convenient, correct packaging of the standard map at its natural generality.
